strings.explore.karsk.wreck.title: The wreck
strings.explore.karsk.wreck.text: The lorry has stood here since the war. One man took the wheels, another the engine, a third the bench seat. The rust is taking the rest. This is what reconstruction looks like from below.
strings.explore.karsk.barrack.title: The barrack
strings.explore.karsk.barrack.text: The barrack is older than half the town. It was built by a “special contingent” – so the sign over the door said, until it was unscrewed in fifty-six. The screw holes are still in the wood. Four families live there now, and the stovepipes go out through the windows.
strings.explore.karsk.cat.title: Pjatiletka
strings.explore.karsk.cat.text: A ginger cat has curled up next to the fire barrel, where the warmth stays near the ground. The men call her Pjatiletka, after the Five-Year Plan: she gets rounder every year, and nobody knows on what. I scratch her behind the ears. She raises her head and allows it – with reservations.
strings.explore.karsk.stairs_under.title: Chess under the stairs
strings.explore.karsk.stairs_under.text: Behind loose bricks under the signal-box stairs: a bundle in oilcloth, tied with a red rag. Inside, a peg chess set, the game in mid-play – day shift against night shift, one move per shift, since October. The night shift is better placed. I’m day shift, and I touch nothing.
strings.explore.karsk.loudspeaker.title: The voice from the mast
strings.explore.karsk.loudspeaker.text: Since six o’clock the loudspeakers on the mast have been announcing the passenger train to Sverdlovsk every twenty minutes. The word “delay” occurs in none of the announcements. We don’t have delays. We only have trains that aren’t here yet.
strings.explore.karsk.newspaper.title: Karskaya Pravda
strings.explore.karsk.newspaper.text: Yesterday’s “Karskaya Pravda”, wet from the snow at the edges, stamped by the depot library. Page three again carries the commission’s report on the dead in the Katyn forest, with the same photo as every year. Whoever has the truth needn’t reprint it every year.
strings.explore.karsk.cooling_towers.title: Towers in the haze
strings.explore.karsk.cooling_towers.text: The cooling towers are steaming as always. They remind me of Wolodja from the technical college, who went to a town with no name in fifty-seven – just a PO box number in the Urals. In the autumn his letters stopped. The next one came only in spring and said nothing, at great length.
strings.explore.karsk.wagon_chalk.title: Chalk on 24-311
strings.explore.karsk.wagon_chalk.text: On the boards of 24-311, chalk marks over chalk marks, each shift with its own. Right at the bottom, almost washed out: a forty and the abbreviation for “people”. The wagon has been in service since 1931. It hasn’t always carried only freight.
strings.explore.karsk.grain.title: The granary
strings.explore.karsk.grain.text: Five silos, one with a patched shell hole. From here the grain goes west with the corridor delivery; the queue stays outside the bread shop. To this day my mother picks every grain up off the floor. She was eighteen in the winter of thirty-three and never speaks of it.
strings.explore.karsk.snowman.title: Snowman on duty
strings.explore.karsk.snowman.text: Someone has put a tin can on the snowman for an ushanka, and a child’s sledge stands beside him. The nose is a bolt – there won’t be carrots again until spring. He stands straighter than half the night shift and has never once asked about his pay.
strings.explore.karsk.banner.title: Painted over
strings.explore.karsk.banner.text: “Together we rebuild” – fresh paint on old cloth. An older slogan shows through underneath, with a name in it that has been carefully painted over. Here, slogans outlive their heroes.
strings.explore.karsk.crows.title: Inspectors in grey
strings.explore.karsk.crows.text: The hooded crows on the loudspeaker cable watch the shunting like inspectors from the ministry: grey coat, black cap, unimpressed. They are wary of people. Never of trains – they know better than the timetable which ones really come.
strings.explore.karsk.stash.title: Music on ribs
strings.explore.karsk.stash.text: Well hidden, where nobody sweeps: a tin. Inside, an X-ray, cut round, with fine grooves – someone’s ribcage, with jazz on it. Lungs: clear. Music: unlicensed. I put everything back the way it was.
strings.explore.karsk.kontora_shelf.title: The missing binder
strings.explore.karsk.kontora_shelf.text: On the shelf in the kontora the binders stand by year. At 1939 only a label is left: “Border stations, handover – additional protocol”. The binder itself is missing; only its rim of dust remains. Here, it’s always the additional part that goes missing.
strings.explore.karsk.mitten.title: A single mitten
strings.explore.karsk.mitten.text: A red child’s mitten, pulled over a fence post. Someone found it in the snow and stuck it up there so its owner will find it. Karsk has no lost-property office. It has fence posts.
strings.explore.karsk.flatcar.title: Panels for happiness
strings.explore.karsk.flatcar.text: Wall panels for the new five-storey blocks, series 1-464: no lift, thin walls, a bathroom the size of a wardrobe. Whoever gets a flat in one moves in with flowers all the same. Mother and I would too – if our turn ever comes.
strings.explore.karsk.distant_train.title: Trains without lights
strings.explore.karsk.distant_train.text: On the bypass line, trains sometimes run without lights and without a whistle: sealed wagons, always heading east. They aren’t in any timetable I know. And yet the rails there are worn shiny.
strings.explore.karsk.vendor.title: Tea without sugar
strings.explore.karsk.vendor.text: The tea seller has hot tea, no sugar and no answers. At night the hatch stays shut.
strings.explore.karsk.vendor.l1: Tea, Engineer? Sugar’s for regulars only now. A regular is anyone who didn’t get any yesterday either.
strings.explore.karsk.vendor.l3: For years. Here – no sugar, but hot.
strings.explore.karsk.vendor.l4: They say a train came through last night. No lights. Did you see it?
strings.explore.karsk.vendor.l5: At night I shut the hatch. Tea tastes better when you’ve seen nothing.
strings.explore.karsk.vendor.l6: And if you did see something?
strings.explore.karsk.vendor.l7: Then you drink it faster. Or you ask the night shift – they’re brooding over their chess under the signal-box stairs anyway.
strings.explore.karsk.workers.title: At the fire barrel
strings.explore.karsk.workers.text: Butter is getting dearer, and so is the quota. Whoever complains is in no newspaper. Whoever asks gets transferred – voluntarily, says the transfer slip.
strings.explore.karsk.workers.l1: Morning, Engineer. Butter’s gone up again. So has the quota, by the way. Only the wages stay stable.
strings.explore.karsk.workers.l3: Mischa’s brother complained. Sixty-two, at a locomotive works in the south – with pictures of Lenin, in front of the party building.
strings.explore.karsk.workers.l5: It’s in no newspaper. So nothing happened. Mischa hasn’t said much since.
strings.explore.karsk.workers.l6: And Kolja asked about the rebooked wagons last week. Now he’s shovelling snow on the northern line. Voluntarily, it says on the transfer slip.
strings.explore.karsk.workers.l8: Numbers are the most dangerous thing, Engineer. Numbers can be checked.
strings.explore.karsk.family.title: Waiting for Sverdlovsk
strings.explore.karsk.family.text: An old woman and her grandchild have been waiting since yesterday for the train to Sverdlovsk. It is no longer on the board.
strings.explore.karsk.family.l1: The train to Sverdlovsk, sonny? We’ve been waiting since early yesterday.
strings.explore.karsk.family.l2: It isn’t on the board any more.
strings.explore.karsk.family.l3: Boards. In forty-one I waited three days for a train that wasn’t on any board. It came all the same.
strings.explore.karsk.family.l4: My grandchild wants to know if you’re the man who makes the signals green.
strings.explore.karsk.family.l6: Then make one green for us. We promised to be on time.
strings.explore.karsk.family.l7: I’ll see what I can do.
strings.explore.karsk.family.l8: Don’t promise anything, sonny. Others have done that before.
strings.explore.karsk.shunting.title: The evening train
strings.explore.karsk.shunting.text: Four wagons, three tracks, one locomotive and a slip with the right order. The shunter drank tea the whole time and showed me the points with his whistle. Now the evening train stands exactly as it says on the slip, and tomorrow his name will be under it.
strings.explore.karsk.chess.title: Mate in two
strings.explore.karsk.chess.text: The night shift was better placed until the day shift gave up its queen. I made two moves for the day shift and tipped over the black king, as is proper. I’m day shift. This time I touched something.
